subject: maths
title: Integers and Negative Numbers: Number Lines, Ordering and Counting across Zero
seo_title: Year 6 Integers Worksheets: Negative Numbers, Number Lines and Ordering (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Recognise situations, including financial contexts, that use integers; locate and represent integers on a number line and as coordinates on the Cartesian plane
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on integers for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N01): negative numbers in temperatures, sea level and bank balances, reading number lines, comparing and ordering integers, and counting across zero. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Negative numbers are to the left of 0, so −7 < −2.
key_sub: Below zero, below sea level and money owed are negative. The farther left on the number line, the smaller the number. When you count across zero, 0 counts as a step.
body_html:
What are integers?

Integers are the whole numbers, their negatives and 0: … −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 … A negative number has a minus sign. −8 is read “negative 8”.

Integers describe two opposite directions. 0 is the starting point between them. It is neither positive nor negative.

SituationPositive0 meansNegative
Temperatureabove zero: 12 °Cwater freezesbelow zero: −5 °C
Heightabove sea level: 2228 msea levelbelow sea level: −15 m
Moneysaved: $20nothing saved or owedowing: −$15
Liftlevel 3ground floorcar park: level −2
Example 1

At 6 am in Thredbo, it is 4 degrees below zero. Which integer shows the temperature?

“Below zero” is the negative direction.

Answer: −4 °C

Integers on a number line

Positive integers are to the right of 0. Negative integers are to the left. Before you read a point, work out what each tick mark is worth.

Compare and order integers

The farther left a number is, the smaller it is. So every negative number is less than 0, and −7 is less than −2.

Example 2

Order from smallest to largest: 3, −5, 0, −8

Start with the number farthest left. −8 is farther left than −5.

Answer: −8, −5, 0, 3

Count on and back across zero

Counting on (a rise, a deposit, going up) moves right. Counting back (a fall, spending, going down) moves left. When you pass 0, 0 counts as a step.

Example 3

Zara has $10 in her account. She pays a $25 bill, and the balance goes below zero. What is her balance?

Count back 25 from 10: 10 takes you to $0, then 15 more.

Answer: −$15 (she owes $15)

Integers are also used as coordinates on the Cartesian plane, such as (−3, 2), where −3 means 3 units left of the origin.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 15 for “owing $15”Owing, below zero, below sea level and spending are negative: −15
−7 > −2 because 7 > 2Farther left is smaller: −7 < −2
Counting each tick as 1 when the scale counts by 2 or 5Find the tick value first: label difference ÷ spaces
Skipping 0: −3 up 5 is 3Count 0 as a step: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2
From −3 to 4 is 1 stepGo through 0: 3 steps to 0, then 4 more, so 7 steps

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about integers in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 6 (AC9M6N01) students recognise situations that use integers, including money, and locate and represent integers on a number line and as coordinates on the Cartesian plane. Adding and subtracting integers comes in Year 7.

faq.q: How do you explain negative numbers to a Year 6 child?
faq.a: Negative numbers show the opposite direction from 0, like below zero on a thermometer, below sea level or money you owe. On a number line they are to the left of 0.
−7 is smaller. It is farther left on the number line, just as −7 °C is colder than −2 °C, so −7 < −2.

faq.q: How do you count across zero on a number line?
faq.a: Count one step at a time and include 0. From −3, counting on 5 goes −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, so you land on 2.

items.q: On a July morning in Thredbo, the temperature at 6 am was 6 degrees below zero. By 2 pm, it was 3 degrees above zero. Which integer represents the temperature at 6 am?
items.e: Below zero is the negative direction, so the integer is −6. Here, 0 would mean 0 °C. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: On the Great Barrier Reef, a diver is 9 metres below sea level. A seagull flies 14 metres above sea level. Which integer represents the diver’s position?
items.e: Below sea level is the negative direction, so the integer is −9. Here, 0 would mean sea level. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: Mei’s bank account changed twice. On Monday, she made a deposit of $35. On Friday, she made a withdrawal of $20. Which integer represents the Friday change to the account?
items.e: A withdrawal is the negative direction, so the integer is −20. Here, 0 would mean no change to the account. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: In a Brisbane shopping centre, the car park is 2 levels below the ground floor. The cinema is 4 levels above the ground floor. Which integer represents the level of the car park?
items.e: Below the ground floor is the negative direction, so the integer is −2. Here, 0 would mean the ground floor. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: In a round of golf, Ethan finished 3 strokes over par and Charlotte finished 2 strokes under par. Which integer represents Charlotte’s score compared with par?
items.e: Under par is the negative direction, so the integer is −2. Here, 0 would mean par. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: On a winter day in Canberra, the temperature at 7 am was 4 degrees below zero. At 3 pm, it was 12 degrees above zero. Which integer represents the temperature at 3 pm?
items.e: Above zero is the positive direction, so the integer is 12. Here, 0 would mean 0 °C.

items.q: On Saturday, Leo earned $18 for washing the car. On Sunday, he spent $11 at the school fete. Which integer represents the money spent on Sunday?
items.e: Spending is the negative direction, so the integer is −11. Here, 0 would mean no change. Do not drop the minus sign.

items.q: In a class quiz, a team wins 10 points for a right answer and loses 5 points for a wrong answer. Which integer represents a right answer?
items.e: Winning points is the positive direction, so the integer is 10. Here, 0 would mean no change to the score.

items.q: Heights are measured in metres above or below sea level. What does a height of 0 m mean?
c: at the top of a mountain
at the bottom of the ocean
there is no height to measure
items.e: Above sea level is positive and below sea level is negative. 0 m is the starting point between them: exactly at sea level.

items.q: A thermometer shows degrees Celsius (°C). What does 0 °C mean?
c: the temperature at which water freezes
the temperature at which water boils
items.e: Water freezes at 0 °C. Colder temperatures are negative, so 0 °C is not the coldest possible: water freezes at 0 °C.

items.q: In a lift, the levels below the ground floor are negative. What does level 0 mean?
c: a level that does not exist
items.e: Levels above the ground floor are positive and levels below it are negative. 0 is the level between them: the ground floor.

items.q: A bank account balance can be positive or negative. What does a balance of $0 mean?
c: no money in the account and nothing owed
items.e: A positive balance is money you have. A negative balance is money you owe. $0 is between them: no money in the account and nothing owed.

items.q: Which situation could the integer −18 represent?
items.e: A negative integer shows the direction below or less than 0. A withdrawal of $18 matches −18. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the integer −25 represent?
items.e: A negative integer shows the direction below or less than 0. Owing $25 matches −25. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the integer −40 represent?
items.e: A negative integer shows the direction below or less than 0. 40 metres below sea level matches −40. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the integer −5 represent?
items.e: A negative integer shows the direction below or less than 0. 5 degrees below zero matches −5. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative integer?
items.e: Spending $12 is the opposite of earning $12, so it is written as −12. The other three are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative integer?
items.e: 4 strokes under par is the opposite of 4 strokes over par, so it is written as −4. The other three are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative integer?
items.e: 3 levels below the ground floor is the opposite of 3 levels above the ground floor, so it is written as −3. The other three are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative integer?
items.e: Losing 6 points is the opposite of winning 6 points, so it is written as −6. The other three are positive.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −2, so A = −3. A is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −4, so A = −5. A is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −6, so A = −7. A is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of 0, so A = −1. A is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −8, so A = −9. A is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the left of −5, so A = −7. Count left from −5: the numbers get smaller as you go left.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the right of −5, so A = −3. Count left from 0, not right.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the right of −10, so A = −8. Count left from −5: the numbers get smaller as you go left.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −5, so A = −6. Count left from −5: the numbers get smaller as you go left.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the right of −5, so A = −4. Count left from 0, not right.

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 10, so each tick mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −2, −4, −6. A = −6. (Counting each tick as 1 gives −3.)

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 25, so each tick mark is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −5, −10, −15. A = −15. (Counting each tick as 1 gives −3.)

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 50, so each tick mark is 50 ÷ 5 = 10. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −10, −20, −30. A = −30. (Counting each tick as 1 gives −3.)

items.q: What integer is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 25, so each tick mark is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Point A is 4 tick marks to the left of 0: −5, −10, −15, −20. A = −20. (Counting each tick as 1 gives −4.)

items.q: Which point is at −5?
items.e: −5 is 5 units to the left of 0. Point B is there. The point at 5 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −3?
items.e: −3 is 3 units to the left of 0. Point C is there. The point at 3 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −7?
items.e: −7 is 7 units to the left of 0. Point A is there. The point at 7 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −2?
items.e: −2 is 2 units to the left of 0. Point D is there. The point at 2 is to the right of 0.

items.q: A thermometer at Perisher shows this temperature. What is it?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 10, so each tick mark is 2 degrees. The red column ends 2 tick marks below 0: −2, −4. The temperature is −4 °C.

items.q: A thermometer at Thredbo shows this temperature. What is it?
items.e: There are 3 spaces between 0 and 15, so each tick mark is 5 degrees. The red column ends 2 tick marks below 0: −5, −10. The temperature is −10 °C.

items.q: Which integer is the greatest? −6, 2, −9, −1
items.e: The greatest number is the one farthest to the right on a number line. 2 is the farthest right, so it is the greatest: 2.

items.q: Which integer is the greatest? −3, −8, −1, −6
items.e: The greatest number is the one farthest to the right on a number line. All four are negative, so the one closest to 0 is the greatest: −1. −8 is the smallest even though 8 is the biggest digit.

items.q: Which integer is the greatest? −12, −5, −9, −2
items.e: The greatest number is the one farthest to the right on a number line. All four are negative, so the one closest to 0 is the greatest: −2. −12 is the smallest even though 12 is the biggest digit.

items.q: Which integer is the greatest? −4, 0, −7, −10
items.e: The greatest number is the one farthest to the right on a number line. 0 is the farthest right, so it is the greatest: 0. 0 is greater than every negative number.

items.q: Which integer is the greatest? −15, −11, −20, −13
items.e: The greatest number is the one farthest to the right on a number line. All four are negative, so the one closest to 0 is the greatest: −11. −20 is the smallest even though 20 is the biggest digit.

items.q: Which integer is the smallest? −2, 1, −9, −5
items.e: The smallest number is the one farthest to the left on a number line. −9 is the farthest left: −9. −2 is greater than −9 because it is closer to 0.

items.q: Which integer is the smallest? −3, −1, 0, 2
items.e: The smallest number is the one farthest to the left on a number line. −3 is the farthest left: −3. −1 is greater than −3 because it is closer to 0.

items.q: Which integer is the smallest? −14, −8, −17, −11
items.e: The smallest number is the one farthest to the left on a number line. −17 is the farthest left: −17. −8 is greater than −17 because it is closer to 0.

items.q: Which integer is the smallest? 4, −4, −6, 6
items.e: The smallest number is the one farthest to the left on a number line. −6 is the farthest left: −6. −4 is greater than −6 because it is closer to 0.

items.q: Which integer is the smallest? −7, −2, −10, −5
items.e: The smallest number is the one farthest to the left on a number line. −10 is the farthest left: −10. −2 is greater than −10 because it is closer to 0.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: −7 is to the left of −2 on a number line, so −7 is smaller: −7 < −2. Do not compare the digits only: 7 > 2, but −7 < −2.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: −10 is to the left of −3 on a number line, so −10 is smaller: −3 > −10. Do not compare the digits only: 10 > 3, but −10 < −3.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: −6 is to the left of 0 on a number line, so −6 is smaller: 0 > −6. Every negative number is less than 0.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: −12 is to the left of −11 on a number line, so −12 is smaller: −12 < −11. Do not compare the digits only: 12 > 11, but −12 < −11.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest? −2, 3, −8, −5
items.e: Start with the number farthest left on a number line. The negative number with the biggest digits is the smallest: −8, −5, −2, 3.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest? −1, −6, 4, 0
items.e: Start with the number farthest left on a number line. The negative number with the biggest digits is the smallest: −6, −1, 0, 4.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest? 5, −9, −3, 1
items.e: Start with the number farthest left on a number line. The negative number with the biggest digits is the smallest: −9, −3, 1, 5.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest? −4, 7, −10, −7
items.e: Start with the number farthest left on a number line. The negative number with the biggest digits is the smallest: −10, −7, −4, 7.

items.q: How many integers are between −3 and 2? (Do not count −3 or 2.)
items.e: List them: −2, −1, 0, 1. That is 4 integers. Do not forget 0: it is an integer too.

items.q: Which integer is between −6 and −2 on a number line?
items.e: −6 and −2 are both to the left of 0. The integers between them are −5, −4 and −3, so the answer is −4. 4 is to the right of 0, so it is not between them.

sets.title: Count on and back across zero

items.q: Start at −4 on a number line. Count on 7. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting on moves to the right. From −4 to 0 is 4 steps, then 3 steps more: −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. You land on 3. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at −6 on a number line. Count on 8. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting on moves to the right. From −6 to 0 is 6 steps, then 2 steps more: −5, −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. You land on 2. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at −2 on a number line. Count on 7. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting on moves to the right. From −2 to 0 is 2 steps, then 5 steps more: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. You land on 5. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at −9 on a number line. Count on 13. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting on moves to the right. From −9 to 0 is 9 steps, then 4 steps more: −8, −7, −6, −5, −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. You land on 4. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at −3 on a number line. Count on 4. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting on moves to the right. From −3 to 0 is 3 steps, then 1 step more: −2, −1, 0, 1. You land on 1. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at 3 on a number line. Count back 7. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting back moves to the left. From 3 to 0 is 3 steps, then 4 steps more: 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4. You land on −4. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at 5 on a number line. Count back 8. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting back moves to the left. From 5 to 0 is 5 steps, then 3 steps more: 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3. You land on −3. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at 2 on a number line. Count back 6. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting back moves to the left. From 2 to 0 is 2 steps, then 4 steps more: 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4. You land on −4. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at 1 on a number line. Count back 9. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting back moves to the left. From 1 to 0 is 1 step, then 8 steps more: 0, −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7, −8. You land on −8. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: Start at 4 on a number line. Count back 11. Where do you land?
items.e: Counting back moves to the left. From 4 to 0 is 4 steps, then 7 steps more: 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7. You land on −7. Count 0 as a step.

items.q: At 5 am in Thredbo, the temperature was −5 °C. By 11 am, it had risen 8 degrees. What was the new temperature?
items.e: Rising means counting up 8 degrees from −5 °C: −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The new temperature is 3 °C. Do not skip 0 °C.

items.q: In Canberra, the temperature was 4 °C at 9 pm. Overnight, it fell 7 degrees. What was the new temperature?
items.e: Falling means counting down 7 degrees from 4 °C: 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3. The new temperature is −3 °C. Do not skip 0 °C.

items.q: At Perisher, the temperature was −7 °C at dawn. By lunchtime, it had risen 4 degrees. What was the new temperature?
items.e: Rising means counting up 4 degrees from −7 °C: −6, −5, −4, −3. The new temperature is −3 °C.

items.q: At Falls Creek, the temperature was 2 °C at 4 pm. By midnight, it had fallen 6 degrees. What was the new temperature?
items.e: Falling means counting down 6 degrees from 2 °C: 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4. The new temperature is −4 °C. Do not skip 0 °C.

items.q: On Mount Hotham, the temperature was −8 °C at 6 am. By 1 pm, it had risen 10 degrees. What was the new temperature?
items.e: Rising means counting up 10 degrees from −8 °C: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The new temperature is 2 °C. Do not skip 0 °C.

items.q: How many steps is it from −5 to 3 on a number line?
items.e: From −5 up to 0 is 5. From 0 to 3 is 3. 5 + 3 = 8. (Taking away the digits, 5 − 3, ignores the signs.)

items.q: How many degrees warmer is 4 °C than −3 °C?
items.e: From −3 up to 0 is 3. From 0 to 4 is 4. 3 + 4 = 7. (Taking away the digits, 4 − 3, ignores the signs.)

items.q: How many steps is it from −2 to 7 on a number line?
items.e: From −2 up to 0 is 2. From 0 to 7 is 7. 2 + 7 = 9. (Taking away the digits, 7 − 2, ignores the signs.)

items.q: How many degrees warmer is 4 °C than −9 °C?
items.e: From −9 up to 0 is 9. From 0 to 4 is 4. 9 + 4 = 13. (Taking away the digits, 9 − 4, ignores the signs.)

items.q: The temperature fell from 6 °C to −5 °C. How many degrees did it fall?
items.e: From −5 up to 0 is 5. From 0 to 6 is 6. 5 + 6 = 11. (Taking away the digits, 6 − 5, ignores the signs.)

items.q: Zara has $20 saved. Lachlan owes his mum $15. Which pair of integers shows Zara’s and Lachlan’s money, in order?
items.e: Money saved is positive and money owed is negative: Zara 20, Lachlan −15. 20 and −15.

items.q: Aarav’s bank account balance is −$40. What does this mean?
items.e: A balance of $0 means no money and nothing owed. A negative balance means money is owed: Aarav owes the bank $40.

items.q: Chloe has $25 in her bank account. She pays a $40 bill, and the bank lets the balance go below zero. What is the balance now?
items.e: Count back 40 from 25: 25 takes you to $0, then 15 more takes you to −$15. The balance is −$15 (owing $15).

items.q: Isla’s bank balance is −$30. She puts in $50 from her birthday money. What is the balance now?
items.e: Count on 50 from −30: 30 takes you to $0, then 20 more. The balance is $20.

items.q: Four students wrote their bank balances: Cooper −$12, Ava −$45, Kai $8, Ruby −$30. Who owes the most money?
items.e: The balance farthest below $0 shows the most money owed. −$45 is less than −$30 and −$12, so Ava owes the most.

items.q: Sienna owes a friend $12. She pays back $8. Which integer shows her money situation now, in dollars?
items.e: Owing $12 is −12. Paying back $8 moves 8 towards 0: −12 to −4. She still owes $4: −4.

items.q: Mount Kosciuszko is 2228 m above sea level. Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre is about 15 m below sea level. Which pair of integers shows their heights, in order?
items.e: Above sea level is positive and below sea level is negative: 2228 and −15.

items.q: Liam is snorkelling at −12 m. He swims up 5 m. What integer shows his new position?
items.e: Up means counting towards 0: −11, −10, −9, −8, −7. Liam is now at −7 m, still below sea level.

items.q: These were the 6 am temperatures in Thredbo one week in July: Monday −6 °C, Tuesday −2 °C, Wednesday 0 °C, Thursday −9 °C. Which morning was the coldest?
items.e: The coldest temperature is the one farthest below 0. −9 °C is colder than −6 °C, so Thursday was the coldest.

items.q: At 6 am one July morning: Canberra −4 °C, Thredbo −9 °C, Hobart 2 °C, Sydney 8 °C. Which list goes from coldest to warmest?
items.e: Coldest means farthest left on a number line: −9 °C, −4 °C, 2 °C, 8 °C. Thredbo, Canberra, Hobart, Sydney. −9 °C is colder than −4 °C.

items.q: Oliver parks on the level marked “car”. He takes the lift up 5 levels to the cinema. Which level is the cinema on?
items.e: The car is on level −2. Count up 5 levels: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The cinema is on level 3. Level 0 (the ground floor) counts as a level.

items.q: Grace is on level 3 of a hospital. She takes the lift down 5 levels to the car park. Which level is the car park?
items.e: Count down 5 levels from 3: 2, 1, 0, −1, −2. The car park is on level −2. Do not skip level 0.

items.q: In Canberra, the temperature was 2 °C at 6 pm and −5 °C at 3 am. How many degrees did it fall?
items.e: From 2 down to 0 is 2 degrees. From 0 down to −5 is 5 degrees. 2 + 5 = 7 degrees.

items.q: The lowest temperature ever recorded in Australia is −23 °C, at Charlotte Pass in New South Wales. One winter morning in Canberra was −5 °C. How many degrees colder is the record?
items.e: Both are below 0. From −5 down to −23 is 23 − 5 = 18 degrees. Do not add 23 and 5: both temperatures are on the same side of 0.

items.q: In golf, par is 0. Matilda finished 4 strokes under par. Mia finished 1 stroke over par. Which integer shows Matilda’s score?
items.e: Under par is negative and over par is positive. Matilda is 4 under par: −4. (Mia’s score is 1.)

items.q: A freezer is set to −18 °C. The fridge is 4 °C. How many degrees colder is the freezer than the fridge?
items.e: From 4 down to 0 is 4 degrees. From 0 down to −18 is 18 degrees. 4 + 18 = 22 degrees.

items.q: William owes his dad $8. He earns $5 doing chores and gives it all to his dad. Which integer shows his money situation now, in dollars?
items.e: Owing $8 is −8. Paying back $5 moves 5 towards 0: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3. He still owes $3: −3.

items.q: Amelia’s bank balance is −$20. Mei’s balance is −$35. Which statement is true?
c: Neither of them owes any money.
They have the same amount of money.
items.e: −20 is closer to 0 than −35, so −20 > −35. Amelia has more money: she owes less.

items.q: An Australasian gannet is flying 6 m above the sea. It dives down 9 m to catch a fish. What integer shows its position now, in metres compared with sea level?
items.e: Count down 9 from 6: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3. The gannet is at −3 m, 3 m below sea level.

items.q: In a class quiz, a team starts on 0 points. They lose 3 points, win 5 points, then lose 4 points. What is their score now?
items.e: 0 back 3 is −3. On 5 is 2. Back 4 is −2. The score is −2.
